selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What did the traveller understand from the oceans and rivers, even though he saw only a very small part of their signs?
questions.answer: He understood that they contain many proofs pointing to Allah’s oneness and necessary existence.

questions.question: How do the seas give their testimony, according to the passage?
questions.answer: They declare Allah’s oneness together and do so with a force that matches their vast size.

questions.question: Who are presented as witnesses supporting the testimony of the seas?
questions.answer: The living creatures and other beings within them are presented as witnesses.

questions.question: What is the main message expressed in the Fourth Degree of the First Station?
questions.answer: All seas and rivers, along with what they contain, point to the existence and unity of Allah.

questions.question: Which qualities of the waters are used as evidence in that testimony?
questions.answer: Their being controlled, safeguarded, stored up, and managed in a wide and orderly way.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention both seas and rivers instead of only one of them?
questions.answer: It shows that different kinds of waters in the world all give the same testimony.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest by saying this order can be observed?
questions.answer: It means these signs are not hidden ideas only; people can notice them in the world itself.

questions.question: What can a reader infer from the link between vastness and order in the waters?
questions.answer: Such large and organized systems are presented as signs of deliberate divine rule, not randomness.

questions.question: How does the traveller’s perception function in this passage?
questions.answer: It serves as a way of recognizing and conveying the meaning found in creation.

questions.question: Summarize the whole target passage in one sentence.
questions.answer: The passage teaches that oceans, rivers, and all they contain visibly show careful order and protection, and therefore testify to Allah’s unity and necessary existence.

questions.question: At the start of the passage, how much of the truths in the oceans and rivers did the traveller see?
questions.answer: He saw only a tiny portion of them.

questions.question: What does this small portion imply about the full reality of the seas and rivers?
questions.answer: It implies that their signs and meanings are far greater than what he was able to notice.

questions.question: What united statement do the seas make?
questions.answer: They affirm that only Allah is worthy of worship.

questions.question: In what way is the strength of that statement described?
questions.answer: It is described as being as powerful as the immensity of the seas themselves.

questions.question: What role do the beings inside the waters play in the argument of the passage?
questions.answer: They strengthen the testimony by serving as evidence that supports it.

questions.question: According to the formal declaration in the passage, what natural things point to Allah’s existence in unity?
questions.answer: All the seas and rivers, together with everything in them, point to it.

questions.question: Which four major patterns in the waters are highlighted as proof?
questions.answer: Their being made subject to command, preserved, stored, and administered in an orderly way.

questions.question: What is the importance of order in the passage’s reasoning?
questions.answer: Order shows wise control and purposeful management rather than chaos.

questions.question: How is observation important to understanding this testimony?
questions.answer: The passage teaches that a person can recognize these truths by reflecting on what is plainly visible in creation.

questions.question: What is the best overall conclusion of the passage?
questions.answer: The world of waters is shown as a clear sign of Allah’s existence, unity, power, and governance.

questions.question: What did the traveller realize after looking at the oceans and rivers?
questions.answer: He realized that they carry many truths affirming Allah, even though he grasped only a little of them.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying the seas speak “unanimously”?
questions.answer: It means they all give one shared testimony without contradiction.

questions.question: What is that shared testimony?
questions.answer: That there is no deity except Allah.

questions.question: How does the passage connect the greatness of the seas with the force of their testimony?
questions.answer: It presents their enormous scale as matching the greatness and strength of the witness they give.
